name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Write persistent compilation cache entries atomically

head_commit.message:
Write persistent compilation cache entries atomically

`LRUCache.put` wrote entries in place with `write_bytes`, so another process
sharing the cache directory could read a partially written entry, and a
process killed mid-write left a truncated entry behind. Since `put` returned
early when the entry already existed, a truncated entry was never replaced:
every later process failed to read it and recompiled.

On local filesystems, `put` now writes the entry to a uniquely named
temporary file in the cache directory, fsyncs it and renames it into place
with `os.replace`, replacing any existing entry. The temporary file is
removed if the write fails. This restores what the old `GFileCache` did.
Remote filesystems keep the previous behaviour, since rename is not atomic
there in general.

Fixes #42197.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Fix jax.scipy.signal.convolve/correlate rejecting mixed-size inputs in full and same modes (#42061)

head_commit.message:
Fix jax.scipy.signal.convolve/correlate rejecting mixed-size inputs in full and same modes (#42061)

In jax._src.scipy.signal._convolve_nd, an unconditional check:
if not (no_swap or swap): raise ValueError(...)
rejected inputs where neither operand was smaller than the other in every
dimension (e.g. shape (8, 2) and (3, 5)).

While this restriction is required for mode='valid', multidimensional
convolution and correlation in mode='full' and mode='same' are mathematically
well-defined for mixed-dimension inputs and supported by SciPy and FFT.

Restrict the check to mode == 'valid', allowing direct and auto
convolution/correlation to handle mixed-size inputs through padding.
Add unit tests verifying numerical parity with SciPy and error checking
for valid mode.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: In `pltpu.emit_pipeline`, `BufferedRef.create` enabled lookahead whenever `pl.Buffered(buffer_count=1, use_lookahead=True)` was passed for an input spec. A single buffered input allocates one VMEM slot and one semaphore, leaving no spare prefetch slot.

head_commit.message:
In `pltpu.emit_pipeline`, `BufferedRef.create` enabled lookahead whenever `pl.Buffered(buffer_count=1, use_lookahead=True)` was passed for an input spec. A single buffered input allocates one VMEM slot and one semaphore, leaving no spare prefetch slot.

Prologue `initialize_step` skips block zero when `in_buffer_count` is one, and `fetch_with_lookahead` starts at block one. Non empty initial blocks stall because lookahead signals fewer bytes than `wait_in` awaits. When step zero transfers a zero length `BoundedSlice`, step zero prefetches step one into slot zero and `advance_slots` increments `cumulative_wait_in`. Step one `copy_in` then runs before `wait_in` and overwrites slot zero with step two.

Gate `_grid_rank` on `use_lookahead and in_buffer_count > 1` so single buffered inputs run synchronously while multi buffered lookahead is unchanged.

display_title: Allow Format in jax.numpy.from_dlpack type annotations and docstring.

head_commit.message:
Allow Format in jax.numpy.from_dlpack type annotations and docstring.

`jax.dlpack.from_dlpack` supports passing a `Format` object to the `device` parameter to specify an explicit device-local layout during DLPack import. Although `jax.numpy.from_dlpack` forwards `device` directly to `jax.dlpack.from_dlpack`, its function signature, type stub, and docstring still restricted `device` to `Device | Sharding | None`.

Extend the `device` type annotation on `jax.numpy.from_dlpack` and its `.pyi` stub to accept `Format`, and update its docstring to document `Format` placement and format-transfer copy behavior.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Raise errors instead of silently computing wrong values when unreduce…

head_commit.message:
Raise errors instead of silently computing wrong values when unreduced/reduced arrays are mixed with constants
On Explicit meshes and inside shard_map, mixing an `unreduced` or `reduced`
array with a replicated constant in pad, concatenate/stack, and select_n could
silently give wrong results. For example, with 4 devices,
`jnp.pad(u, 1, constant_values=1.)` returned `[4., 10., 4.]` instead of
`[1., 10., 1.]`, because every device kept a full copy of the constant and the
final sum counted it 4 times.
* `pad`: `_pad_ur_rule` now requires `operand` and `padding_value` to have the
  same unreduced/reduced axes.
* `concatenate` / `stack` / `select_n`: the unreduced/reduced rules no longer
  skip operands that have no unreduced/reduced axes; all operands (cases for
  select_n) must match. `which` in select_n can't be unreduced.
* `_zero(x)` keeps x's unreduced/reduced axes. The pad and slice transposes
  pad with `_zero(t)` instead of a plain `0`.
* `full` / `full_like`:
  * Explicit mode: an eager concrete sharding with unreduced now goes through
    `broadcast(..., out_sharding=...)`, so it stays unreduced.
  * Inside shard_map: `full_like` applies x's `mat.reduced` and
    `mat.unreduced`. For unreduced, the value is kept on one device and the
    others get 0, so the sum is the fill value.
* `zeros_like_shaped_array` raises for UnreducedKind.max/min instead of
  returning an untagged zero.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Raise errors instead of silently computing wrong values when unreduced/reduced arrays are mixed with constants

head_commit.message:
Raise errors instead of silently computing wrong values when unreduced/reduced arrays are mixed with constants
On Explicit meshes and inside shard_map, mixing an `unreduced` or `reduced`
array with a replicated constant in pad, concatenate/stack, and select_n could
silently give wrong results. For example, with 4 devices,
`jnp.pad(u, 1, constant_values=1.)` returned `[4., 10., 4.]` instead of
`[1., 10., 1.]`, because every device kept a full copy of the constant and the
final sum counted it 4 times.
* `pad`: `_pad_ur_rule` now requires `operand` and `padding_value` to have the
  same unreduced/reduced axes.
* `concatenate` / `stack` / `select_n`: the unreduced/reduced rules no longer
  skip operands that have no unreduced/reduced axes; all operands (cases for
  select_n) must match. `which` in select_n can't be unreduced.
* `_zero(x)` keeps x's unreduced/reduced axes. The pad and slice transposes
  pad with `_zero(t)` instead of a plain `0`.
* `full` / `full_like`:
  * Explicit mode: an eager concrete sharding with unreduced now goes through
    `broadcast(..., out_sharding=...)`, so it stays unreduced.
  * Inside shard_map: `full_like` applies x's `mat.reduced` and
    `mat.unreduced`. For unreduced, the value is kept on one device and the
    others get 0, so the sum is the fill value.
* `zeros_like_shaped_array` raises for UnreducedKind.max/min instead of
  returning an untagged zero.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010974981

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Add a custom JVP rule for jnp.linalg.lstsq

head_commit.message:
Add a custom JVP rule for jnp.linalg.lstsq

lstsq was differentiated through the SVD, whose JVP divides by
s_i**2 - s_j**2. For matrices with repeated singular values (orthonormal
columns, balanced one-hot designs, a symmetric matrix with a repeated
eigenvalue) this gave NaN or wrong gradients.

Apply the Golub-Pereyra derivative of the pseudo-inverse to b instead,
computed from the SVD factors of the forward pass. The forward
computation is unchanged.
